raw_case_text:
A 64-year-old farmer presented with shiny, nonitching nodules, papules, and plaques over various parts of body especially prominent over trunk, lower back, buttocks, arms, and legs but involving face, chest wall, elbow, and knee, counting approximately 42 in number (Figures 1(a)-1(c)). The lesions began as papules over anterior abdominal wall and lower back two months back. The lesions were flat-toped, nonscaly, flesh-colored to erythematous, almost symmetrical, normal-oedematous, soft-firm, 0.3 x 0.3 to 10.0 x 5.5 cm in size, painful for past 15 days. Scalp, ears, oral cavity, palms, soles, and genitalia were spared. There was history of low-grade fever for 15 days, associated with redness, pain and discharge from eye, and nasal stuffiness. Nasal bridge was normal. Nerve thickening and lymph node enlargement were absent. There was no impairment of pain, touch, or temperature sensation. No history of epistaxis/insect-bite/trauma/long-term drug intake was given. Family history was noncontributory. Hematological findings were normal except for mild leukocytosis. ELISA for HIV was negative. The clinical considerations included infective diseases (Kala azar/other granulomatous lesions), sarcoidosis, and acute febrile neutrophilic dermatoses.
Histopathology revealed focal epidermal atrophy with an underlying cellular band. The dermis revealed a large, circumscribed collection of benign spindle cells resembling fibroblasts, arranged in a whorled and storiform pattern, with entrapped but preserved small dermal nerve and adenexal structures. Within the mass of spindle-shaped histiocytes, rounded-polygonal plump histiocytic cells with vacuolated cytoplasm along with occasional giant cells were noticed (Figures 2(a)-2(c)). The possibility of benign fibrohistiocytic lesion was kept. However, Ziehl Neelsen (ZN) staining (5% sulphuric acid) revealed abundant, mostly solid, acid fast bacilli (AFB) within the histiocytes and endothelial cells, as well as lying extracellularly (Figure 2(d)). These bacilli were longer than the normal bacilli, scattered singly as well as arranged in clusters. Slit skin smear revealed acid-fast bacilli with bacteriological index (BI) of 4+ to 5+ and microbiological index (MI) of 60-70%. A final diagnosis of de novo histoid leprosy was made. The patient has been put on multibacillary multidrug therapy (MBMDT) with rifampicin, clofazamine, and dapsone and is on regular followup. In the past eleven-month treatment, the patient has responded well (Figures 1(d) and 1(e)).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 64-year-old male farmer presented with a 2-month history of widespread non-pruritic nodules, papules, and plaques that became painful over the preceding 15 days alongside low-grade fever, ocular redness and discharge, and nasal stuffiness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two months prior to presentation, the patient noticed asymptomatic papules on his anterior abdominal wall and lower back that progressively multiplied to approximately 42 lesions across his trunk, buttocks, extremities, and face. Fifteen days before consultation, the lesions became painful and were accompanied by low-grade fever, ocular pain, redness, and discharge, and nasal congestion.
subjective.past_medical_history: Farmer by occupation; negative family history and no history of epistaxis, insect bites, trauma, or chronic medication use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for lesional pain (15 days), low-grade fever, ocular pain/redness/discharge, and nasal stuffiness; negative for pruritus or epistaxis.

objective.physical_examination: Cutaneous examination revealed approximately 42 nearly symmetrical, flat-topped, non-scaly, flesh-colored to erythematous, soft-to-firm edematous papules, nodules, and plaques (measuring 0.3 x 0.3 cm to 10.0 x 5.5 cm) over the trunk, lower back, buttocks, arms, elbows, legs, knees, and face, sparing the scalp, ears, oral mucosa, palms, soles, and genitalia. The nasal bridge was intact, peripheral nerves and lymph nodes were not enlarged, and pain, light touch, and temperature sensations were preserved.
objective.routine_investigations: Hematological workup was normal except for mild leukocytosis; HIV ELISA was negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Slit-skin smear and lesional skin biopsy with H&E and 5% sulfuric acid Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) staining were performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Skin biopsy revealed focal epidermal atrophy, a subepidermal Grenz zone (cellular band), and a circumscribed dermal proliferation of whorled and storiform spindle-shaped histiocytes and plump vacuolated histiocytes with preserved dermal nerves/adnexa, packed with elongated, solid intracellular and extracellular acid-fast bacilli on 5% ZN staining; slit-skin smear confirmed a Bacteriological Index (BI) of 4+ to 5+ and Morphological Index (MI) of 60-70%, establishing de novo histoid leprosy (ruling out kala-azar/post-kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis, sarcoidosis, sweet syndrome, and benign fibrohistiocytic tumors). He was initiated on multibacillary multidrug therapy (rifampicin, clofazimine, and dapsone) with marked clinical regression over 11 months of follow-up.
